title: Astrid and the Compass
premise: Jude Fairweather, a riverboat captain haunted by the debt she owes to the family of a man who died on her boat, is hired by a desperate widow to find an expedition that vanished above the Weir Line, where the river narrows into territory closed by law and legend. Following the compass her dead father left her — which points not north but toward whatever she most refuses to face — Jude discovers the expedition was hunting proof that the river's source sits on stolen land, evidence powerful men will kill to bury. Betrayed by one ally, saved by another she'd wrongly blamed, Jude must run the calving rapids at the glacier's brief seasonal opening to carry the truth downstream. She wins justice for the vanished expedition and, in choosing truth over loyalty to her own silence, finally pays her debt — though not with money.
about_author: Gideon Galloway spent six years as a deckhand on working riverboats before turning to writing full-time, a period he describes as 'a graduate seminar in weather, patience, and human nature.' He lives in a converted pilot house on the water and writes each morning before the fog lifts.

chapters.title: The Debt Below the Waterline
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. A routine cargo run down the Alder River establishes Jude's mastery of the water and her crushing debt to the Okonkwo family, whose son died when her old boat went down. The chapter ends with Ada Okonkwo arriving at dusk, asking Jude to do the one thing she swore never to do: go back upriver. Emotional beat: guilt dressed up as competence.

chapters.title: What the Widow Bought
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Ada reveals her husband Elias led a survey expedition past the Weir Line and went silent three weeks ago; the authorities refuse to search forbidden waters. Jude takes the contract for reasons she won't name aloud. She loads the boat, hires her old friend Marsh as engineer, and studies her father's strange compass, which trembles whenever she lies. Emotional beat: reluctant commitment.

chapters.title: Past the Weir
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Crossing the Weir Line at night, Jude evades a patrol launch and enters water no chart covers. The river changes — colder, faster, older. They find the expedition's abandoned supply cache, ransacked but with a journal page hidden inside: Elias believed the source lands were fraudulently deeded to the Halloway Timber Company. Emotional beat: wonder curdling into dread.

chapters.title: The Man in the Reeds
chapters.summary: Alternating POV begins: Sefu, the expedition's guide, half-dead and hiding from his own former crewmates. Jude pulls him aboard; he accuses the expedition's financier, Corliss Hale, of sending them upriver as deniable scouts for a land grab — then killing the ones who objected. Marsh vouches for Sefu; Jude doesn't trust him. Emotional beat: uneasy alliance against a common shadow.

chapters.title: Hale's Launch
chapters.summary: Sefu's POV. Flashback chapters within: how Hale's men turned the expedition against itself, how Elias found the survey documents proving the theft, how Sefu fled rather than help bury him. In the present, Hale's armed launch appears behind them on the river. Jude runs the boat through a fog bank to lose them. Emotional beat: the past becoming pursuit.

chapters.title: Marsh's Bargain
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Marsh disappears overnight with the fuel reserve and the journal pages — sold out to Hale, it seems. Stranded, betrayed, Jude nearly turns back, but the compass needle steadies only when she admits why she really came: to prove she isn't the coward who let a man drown. She and Sefu continue on foot along the gorge. Emotional beat: rock bottom, and the choice made there.

chapters.title: The Source
chapters.summary: Sefu's POV. Above the tree line they find the glacial source pool — and Elias, alive but broken, hiding in the survey hut with copies of the deed documents. He explains the calving season will open the meltwater chute for perhaps two days, the only navigable route down. Hale's men are already camped at the chute, waiting. Emotional beat: awe, and the trap revealed.

chapters.title: The Chute Opens
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. The glacier calves; the ice dam groans and splits; the chute floods with a narrow window of runnable water. Jude must retrieve her stranded boat from the cache below while Sefu and Elias hold off Hale's men with flares and nerve. She gets the boat through the first rapid as the ice begins to close. Emotional beat: terror transmuted into purpose.

chapters.title: Compass Point
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Climax. In the narrowing chute, Hale himself boards mid-rapid to seize the documents; Marsh is revealed as a double agent who took the pages to get close enough to copy Hale's confession onto tape. In the chaos of collapsing ice, Marsh saves Jude at the cost of his own life, and Hale's launch founders. Jude rides the last of the meltwater through with the truth intact. Emotional beat: sacrifice, fury, survival.

chapters.title: Downstream
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Resolution. The documents and recording reach the newspapers; the fraudulent deeds collapse and the source lands return to trust. Jude gives Ada the truth about Elias instead of an apology, and the Okonkwos forgive the debt — not because it's paid, but because Jude finally stopped hiding from it. She keeps the compass, its needle now resting easy. Emotional beat: quiet redemption on open water.
